intelligence.essence:
Shawn's eye on the jewel-colors build: "I absolutely love it. It's really, really well done." And then the correction: the bullet points should be ORBS instead — "why wouldn't you just use our orbs that just sort of circled around as the bullet points... we have beautiful orbs right and Smart Factory you can just go there and use them... they would give a better presentation and make it feel alive." The jewel bullets are "okay but... I don't know what they are even." The orbs are ours, they are alive, they circle — a bullet that is a living orb makes the letter feel alive; a bullet that is a pretty stone nobody recognises is decoration without meaning. The colors stay (SN-2405): the orbs wear the digit colors. Orbs + closing seat dispatched by the captain in the same pass.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: right, sn-, words.

I would suggest the orbs instead of those because I don't know what they are even and why wouldn't you just use it we have beautiful orbs right and Smart Factory you can just go there and use them and I just think they would give a better presentation and make it feel alive."
intelligence.child_view: Imagine taking a letter someone wrote by hand and putting it in a beautiful frame — same words, nothing changed, just presented like it matters. Then you check every page turns properly, the button at the end really opens the door, on a big screen and a small phone. Three tiny smudges were found: a missing dash, a line that should be big capital letters, and one extra sentence nobody wrote. All three were told to him honestly, not hidden.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, when someone tells you how to make something beautiful, you listen to what they mean — and then you make it beautiful in your own best words. You don't write their instructions down on the finished thing for everyone to read. The directions are for you. The finished page is for the visitor.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the same law as SN-2409's closing-question order, sharpened by a live failure: dictation carries two things at once — the product words (which stay verbatim) and the direction (which gets shaped). The seat that cannot tell them apart pastes both, and the page reads like a rehearsal. The test is the stranger's eye: "imagine reading that." If the sentence only makes sense as an instruction to a builder, it does not belong on the page. The scorecard step is not optional polish — it is the step that separates material from copy, and skipping it is what produced the defect. The correction compound ran in the same pass (note + interrupt to the seat + PI + GitHub), but the rewrite itself is still pending — the compound is not complete until the crafted close lands and his eye confirms it.
